verses.1: To the Chief Musician, with stringed instruments; a psalm of Asaph, a song.
verses.2: God is known in Judah; his name is great in Israel.
verses.3: His dwelling was in peace, and his tent was in Zion.
verses.4: There he broke the might of the bow, shield and sword and war. There he shattered the horns. Selah.
verses.5: You shine, exalted above the eternal mountains.
verses.6: The hearts of the mighty were struck with fear; their sleep was broken. None among the mighty found their hands.
verses.7: From your rebuke, God of Jacob, both horse and rider were thrown into confusion.
verses.8: You are awesome; who can stand before your anger?
verses.9: From heaven you announced judgment; the earth feared and was still.
verses.10: When God arose to judgment, to save all the humble in the land. Selah.
verses.11: For the intent of man will honor you; the leftover intent will be a feast for you.
verses.12: Make vows and repay to the LORD your God; let all around him bring gifts.
verses.13: He who silences the breath of rulers is terrible to the kings of the earth.

notes:
Notes
- v. 11: "the leftover intent will be a feast for you" reflects the poetic balance of "the intent of man will honor you" and the Hebrew's play on the root of נֶדֶר (vow/intent) and its remainder (שְׁאֵרִית). The reference to "feast" (חֵמֹת) is a poetic rendering of the term, which can also mean "offering" or "gift."
